Q: Cannot include both files (WinSock2, Windows.h) A:

Make sure that <windows.h> doesn't include <winsock.h> (which provides many of the same declarations as <winsock2.h>). In the <winsock2.h> file on my system there is this line:

#define _WINSOCKAPI_   /* Prevent inclusion of winsock.h in windows.h */

The _WINSOCKAPI_ include guard may be an internal implementation detail, but as a practical solution I would rely on it, just defining this symbol before including <windows.h>, e.g. in the compiler invocation (which for an IDE means in the IDE project settings).

Alternatively you can try to always include <winsock2.h> before <windows.h>, in order to establish the relevant include guard whatever it is (but this is I think much more fragile than just assuming that the above guard is practically well-defined);

or you can define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN, which prevents <windows.h> from including <winsock.h> but also some other headers (listing from source on my system those are <cderr.h>, <dde.h>, <ddeml.h>, <dlgs.h>, <lzexpand.h>, <mmsystem.h>, <nb30.h>, <rpc.h>, <shellapi.h>, <winperf.h>, <wincrypt.h>, <winefs.h>, <winscard.h>, <winspool.h>, <ole2.h>, and <commdlg.h>). I do not recommend relying on WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN optimization for correctness.

I.e., minimum:

#undef UNICODE
#define UNICODE
#undef _WINSOCKAPI_
#define _WINSOCKAPI_
#include <windows.h>
#include <winsock2.h>

auto main()
    -> int
{}

Q: Is it possible to check if a session has been created? A:

With the help of Lonami, I was able to solve my problem. With client.iter_messages(chat), I could only view messages, while the "message" I was looking for was an UpdateServiceNotification, so I used events.Raw to get all types of updates.

Here is the code:

from telethon.sync import TelegramClient, events
from telethon.tl.types import UpdateServiceNotification
api_id = 123456
api_hash = "42132142c132145ej"

with TelegramClient('anon', api_id, api_hash) as client:
   @client.on(events.Raw(func = lambda e: type(e) == UpdateServiceNotification))
   async def handler(event):
      print("New Login!")
   client.run_until_disconnected()

Q: RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'UserMethods.get_me' was never awaited A:

You need to use await:

import decouple
from telethon import TelegramClient

client = TelegramClient('testSesh', decouple.config('API_ID_TEST'), decouple.config('API_HASH_TEST'))

async def main():
    await client.start()
    print(await client.get_me())

client.loop.run_until_complete(main())

start() is special-cased in v1 to not need the await but it's generally better if you write all your code inside an async def and not rely on this magic.

Q: How can I represent $\mathbb{character}$ in Github markdown? A:

I have a hack for the $\mathbb{}$ issue in Markdown files in GitHub, not a permanent solution, though.

1)Copy Blackboard bold 'Unicode symbol' characters from Wikipedia

2)Write LaTeX code, instead of $n \in \mathbb{R}$ copy and paste ℝ directly on code $n \in ℝ$

Do not copy LaTeX codes from Wikipedia, it will appear like {\displaystyle \mathbb {R} } . Copy unicode characters only (ℂ, ℍ, ℕ, ℙ, ℚ, ℝ, and ℤ)

Q: Disable developer mode extensions pop up in Chrome A:

Tested environment

  • Windows 10 10.0.19045.6456

  • Microsoft Edge 145.0.3800.70

  • Date: 2026-02-24

This is the method that is already provided by @Antony Hatchkins, @Burak Gök, and @Panther. I just add more description about it.

Processes to use user-developed extensions without the "Disable developer mode extensions" popup:

  1. Enable "Developer Mode" for the Chrome/Edge extension

  2. Install your extension using "Load unpacked"

  3. When your extension works well, pack it into a *.crx file using "Pack extension"

  4. Remove the unpacked version of the extension

  5. Install the packed version of the extension by dragging the *.crx file into the browser. The installed extension would not be enabled at this point.

  6. Copy the extension ID, which is a long, meaningless alphabet string

  7. Open Windows Registry Editor, regedit.exe

  8. Go to the following based on your browser

    • HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge

    • HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome

  9. Create a key "ExtensionInstallAllowlist" under it

  10. Create a value for each extension

    • Name: 1, 2, 3, ...

    • Value: extension ID

  11. Go back to the browser and check the extension is enabled. Then, disable the extension developer mode.

After the step 10, Windows registry becomes like this:

For Chrome instead of Edge, you first let the Windows control the Chrome policy: https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7532015

References

  • https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/get-started/tutorial/hello-world

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-browser-policies/extensioninstallallowlist

  • https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7532015

  • https://chromeenterprise.google/intl/en_us/policies/#ExtensionInstallAllowlist

Q: Requested setting INSTALLED_APPS, but settings are not configured. You must either define the environment variable DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE A:

In my case I was using uvicorn and a problem like yours was raised. The way to solve it generally includes loading django setup first before anything. For example:
`

import os

from django.core.asgi import get_asgi_application

os.environ.setdefault("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "core.settings")

# loads django first
django_application = get_asgi_application()

# after you can use other commands and modify application variable
from channels.auth import AuthMiddlewareStack  # NOQA
from channels.routing import ProtocolTypeRouter, URLRouter  # NOQA
from channels.security.websocket import AllowedHostsOriginValidator  # NOQA
from django.urls import path  # NOQA

from apps.cameras.consumers import CameraConsumer  # NOQA

application = ProtocolTypeRouter(
    {
        "http": django_application,
        "websocket": AllowedHostsOriginValidator(
            AuthMiddlewareStack(
                URLRouter(
                    [
                        path(
                            "ws/camera/<int:camera_id>/stream-in/<int:index>",
                            CameraConsumer.as_asgi(),
                        ),
                    ]
                )
            )
        ),
    }
)

`

For me it was raised 'cause a circular import was happening and in apps.cameras.consumers it's been imported a model which needs settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL(via get_user_model()) that needs to be previously loaded by django.setup() in get_asgi_application()

Q: Why is my website’s Open Graph image not displaying correctly when sharing articles on Facebook, even though the link sometimes loads? A:

I'm having an issue when sharing article links from my WordPress website on Facebook. The thumbnail image does not display. Sometimes Facebook only shows the link with no image, and other times it shows a gray placeholder box where the image should appear (the title loads, but not the photo).

My site is built with WordPress and uses Yoast SEO. I checked Facebook’s Sharing Debugger, and the Open Graph tags are definitely present and detected correctly.

Here’s an example URL:

https://latinoherald.com/2026/02/23/ice-washington-iglesias-organizaciones-respuesta/

Facebook detects:

fb:app_id: 1525807035632022
og:url: https://latinoherald.com/2026/02/23/ice-washington-iglesias-organizaciones-respuesta/
og:type: article
og:title: Iglesias y organizaciones responden ante el aumento de actividad de ICE en Washington
og:description: Iglesias y organizaciones comunitarias refuerzan medidas ante el incremento de actividad de ICE en WA
og:image: https://latinoherald.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/General-Leo-2-2025-12-29T111225.020.jpg

So Open Graph is working, and Facebook can see the image URL, but the thumbnail still does not render on posts.

This makes me think that Facebook’s crawler can read the meta tags, but something on the server (cache, firewall, hotlink protection, etc.) is blocking Facebook from actually fetching the image file.

My question:
What should I check on the server side to make sure Facebook’s crawler (facebookexternalhit / Facebot) is allowed to access images under /wp-content/uploads/? Are there specific LiteSpeed, Hostinger, or ModSecurity rules known to block Facebook image scrapers?

Any suggestions on how to troubleshoot this would be greatly appreciated.
